rv.q: The situation of Beatrice, a smart and forceful woman in a man’s world, is made all the more plain by Hero’s passivity. The background character of servant Margaret (Matilda Bailes, excellent), a tool in the plot by Pedro’s bastard brother John to discredit Hero and destroy her marriage to Claudio, is given depth and character by Walker.
Ultimately what we’re left with is the taste of love games that can all too easily become bittersweet.

Nonetheless, as a largely upbeat, good vibes, modern dress production in which the cast cavort around in amusing animal masks, it does kind of invite comparisons in which it comes out second best, albeit not heinously so.
While this production has both style and substance, the lack of chemistry between its lovers leaves a sour aftertaste.
Walker’s direction is a masterclass in smooth storytelling.

cn.t: Walker's summery, stylish production delivers a fresh and accessible Much Ado with standout wit from its leads, though tonal inconsistencies and an unremarkable approach keep this fizzy staging from fully capturing the play's complexities.
